nodes.summary: Every endpoint-typed process satisfies the canonical π scope predicate.
nodes.title: Endpoint-typed processes are scoped at the ambient depth

nodes.summary: Typed terms stay in the proved Cong/Step-closed finite fragment.
nodes.title: Endpoint-typed processes lie in the finite linear fragment

nodes.summary: Syntax-directed linear typing. Capabilities never contain preservation or progress assumptions. Protocol heads may be guarded regular protocols.
nodes.title: Linear endpoint typing of π-calculus processes

nodes.summary: Input inversion exposes its owned role, literal payload sort, and continuation context. Passive and delegated names are not conflated.
nodes.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for input

nodes.summary: Completed endpoint slots may be added at nil without creating a communication obligation; active protocols cannot use this rule.
nodes.title: Adding a completed capability at nil preserves typing

nodes.summary: Nil inversion exposes completion and scope of every recorded endpoint.
nodes.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for nil

nodes.summary: Any protocol whose guarded head is completed is admissible at a single nil-owned slot, including completed regular graph cursors.
nodes.title: Nil is typed by a single capability with completed head

nodes.summary: A recorded completed capability is admissible at nil; an active one would fail the completed-context premise.
nodes.title: Nil is typed by a single done capability

nodes.summary: Output inversion exposes the actual owned subject, distinct payload sort, and literal continuation resources; delegation consumes the payload role.
nodes.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for output

nodes.summary: Every output subject is backed by an owned role, never merely by a passive name in the ambient data scope.
nodes.title: Output subjects of endpoint-typed processes are owned

nodes.summary: Parallel typing exposes an actual disjoint ownership split, not a stored preservation or progress witness.
nodes.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for parallel composition

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
